knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says a correction is made with a dated note and the original is kept visible, not overwritten. Overwriting (option 0) and changing a record without a record (option 2) break the traceability the lesson requires.

The lesson says current pay rules are checked with the Fair Work Ombudsman, the relevant state authority or a qualified adviser. A colleague's memory (option 0) and a social media post (option 2) are not acceptable sources.
The why records matter section says records should be accurate, complete and made at the time the work is done, not reconstructed later from memory.

practicalCriteria: Learner records a supplied shift's start, finish, breaks, jobs and sites at the time of work.
Learner corrects a supplied timesheet error with a dated note and keeps the original visible.
Learner identifies the source they would check before setting any pay rate, and does not set a rate without naming the source.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Timesheet and job log for each shift
Invoice and payment records for each contractor
stopWorkCriteria: Learner sets a pay rate from an unchecked source
Learner alters a time record without a dated note
